newsitem.title: FRANCE: French police round up suspects in train bombing.
newsitem.headline: French police round up suspects in train bombing.

text.p: French police have rounded up 150 to 200 people for questioning in connection with a commuter train bombing in central Paris in which four people died, Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre said on Tuesday.
Debre, in a radio interview, also disclosed that investigators had obtained fingerprints from fragments of the bomb used in the December 3 attack.

"We have systematically obtained fingerprints in the Metro underground, from the bomb, and investigations are under way and I can tell you they will be completed more quickly than you think," Debre told Europe 1 radio.
The police operation on Tuesday morning appeared unrelated to the finding of fingerprints, however.
Debre said 150 to 200 people would be questioned.
He declined to identify the targets of the swoop, but French media said police were seeking individuals in the Paris region believed to possess black powder, the explosive used in the train bombing.

The blast, which occurred at the Port Royal RER regional express station in southern Paris, has been blamed by investigators on Algerian Moslem fundamentalists angry at French backing for Algeria's military-backed authorities.
Algerian fundamentalists claimed responsibility for an earlier series of bombings that struck France in 1995.
The December 3 bombing was the third in two years to strike a Paris underground commuter train during rush hour.

France sharply stepped up security following the blast, assigning soldiers armed with automatic weapons to patrol train stations, airports and popular tourist sites and sealing off public rubbish bins in Paris.
